Long description: For directionless inferential statistics (e.g., p-value, F-value, ?²), assign a sign based on the reference level in the model. If the model’s reference (i.e., the intercept) is the control group, and the treatment group shows a higher value for the outcome, assign +1. If the treatment group shows a lower value than the control, assign –1. This sign should reflect the direction of the effect relative to the reference and must be independent of the Outcome_expected_sign. Both signs must remain separate to prevent them from incorrectly canceling each other out. In practice, the final effect size will be multiplied by both signs to yield the correct overall direction. For more details, refer to the meta-analysis material in 03_effect_size, especially the section titled “Sign matters, A LOT”. Understanding this is crucial—mistakes here can render the dataset invalid.
